hematology_practice.supported_decision: Evaluate isolated adult thrombocytopenia with history/exam, peripheral smear and exclusion of secondary causes; reserve marrow for additional abnormal findings or atypical/refractory clinical presentation.
revision_guidance: Keep vignette adult and without additional cytopenias, dysplastic smear, systemic signs or other features that would justify marrow if correct answer avoids routine marrow.
A platelet count alone is not a confirmed primary ITP diagnosis. Preserve explicit exclusion-based uncertainty.
Do not attach treatment thresholds/doses to a diagnosis-focused item unless separate retained source supports them.
Japanese detailed testing and Spanish general secondary-cause exclusion directly support the decision; no scope-only abstract padding.

oncology_practice.supported_decision: Selected clinically low-risk adult cancer patients may enter an established ambulatory FN pathway after validated clinical risk assessment and disease/treatment/patient safety-net evaluation.
revision_guidance: Keep decision focused on eligibility and disposition. This pair does not establish a universal named drug/dose, fixed time-to-antibiotic interval, minimum observation duration, or exact follow-up schedule.
Include clinically relevant stability, absence of organ dysfunction/severe focal infection, oral tolerance and dependable access/caregiver context; a numerical low-risk score alone is insufficient.
Do not put evaluative phrases such as suitable for outpatient care, low-risk management recommendation, or score interpretation in visible imaging/findings/impression fields.
Specific examples of safety exclusions come from heterogeneous study criteria in systematic-review Table1; do not present all as universally validated mandatory cutoffs.
For chemo/ICI-specific cases MASCC42525130 offers usable abstract-only consensus, with explicit nonvalidation and limited-evidence caveats.

supporting_quotes.quote: It is important to confirm the presence of platelet aggregates in a peripheral blood smear.
Testing should also be performed for H. pylori , HIV, HBV, and HCV, all of which are potentially associated with ITP.
Therefore, exclusion of secondary ITP is based on detailed interviews, physical findings, and test results specific to underlying diseases (e.g. virus tests).

limitations: Adult primary ITP diagnosis; Japanese reference framework adds TPO/IPF biomarkers to address aplastic-anemia differential. Do not require those biomarkers universally.
Do not use isolated low platelets to establish primary ITP before excluding secondary causes. Selective marrow evaluation depends on abnormalities and clinical context.

supporting_quotes.quote: Diagnosis continues to be essentially clinical and based on excluding other causes of thrombocytopenia.
The paradigmatic laboratory finding is isolated thrombocytopenia, and careful examination of the peripheral blood smear is mandatory.

The systematic analysis of bone marrow is not recommended, except in the event that treatment response is inadequate, or when other abnormalities in the peripheral blood smear or the clinical presentation lead us to suspect other disorders.

limitations: Mixed adult/pediatric and special-population article; use the general diagnosis section for this adult evaluation.
Routine marrow is not recommended in uncomplicated isolated thrombocytopenia, with exceptions for other abnormalities or inadequate treatment response.

supporting_quotes.quote: ITP is diagnosed by exclusions, with a hallmark laboratory finding of isolated thrombocytopenia.
Bleeding, family and medication histories and a review of historical investigations are required to gauge the bleeding risk and possible hereditary syndromes.

limitations: Abstract supports exclusion-based diagnosis, bleeding/family/medication history; no detailed marrow or viral-testing recommendation in abstract.

supporting_quotes.quote: Recent clinical practice guidelines have recommended ambulatory management of febrile neutropenia in patients with low risk of complications.
all other clinical trials and observational studies have used the MASCC score, generally with a cutoff of 21 points to define low risk
Available evidence on efficacy, quality of life, and cost-efficiency seems to support ambulatory approaches for low-risk patients with febrile neutropenia.
following good response to the first dose in hospital and early discharge.

limitations: Adult population; excludes studies under age19, though discussion mentions teenagers.
Evidence pertains to selected low-risk cancer patients, mostly solid tumors, with heterogeneous exclusion criteria. Does not justify universal discharge based only on a score.
Included studies vary in antibiotics and observation periods; avoid a definitive drug/dose or fixed observation interval without separately retained support.

supporting_quotes.quote: For adult patients the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer and the Clinical Index of Stable Febrile Neutropenia scores are recommended, whereas for paediatric patients the AUS rule has been prospectively derived and validated in the Australian setting.
These rules are recommended as part of a structured low-risk neutropenic fever care pathway that incorporates additional disease-level, treatment-level and patient-level safety net criteria.

limitations: Mixed adult and pediatric guidance; abstract explicitly recommends MASCC/CISNE for adults and AUS for children.
Abstract supports a structured low-risk pathway plus disease/treatment/patient safety-net criteria. It does not give exact antimicrobial choices, dose, or numerical discharge/follow-up intervals.
No PMCID in PubMed metadata; no full-text license asserted. Abstract-only use under existing PubMed pipeline.

supporting_quotes.quote: Management of patients with low-risk FN in an outpatient setting is proven to be safe and effective.
patients with a score ≥ 21 are likely to be suitable for outpatient management.

Patients treated with chemotherapy/ICI therapy with low-risk FN should be treated on the same pathway as those treated with chemotherapy alone with inclusion criteria adapted to recognise their eligibility.

limitations: Actual fullTextXML CC BY-NC-ND4; retain only PubMed abstract.

Primarily chemotherapy plus immune-checkpoint-inhibitor cohort; abstract says MASCC not validated for combined chemo/ICI and notes only one eligible literature paper. Distinguish consensus extrapolation from validated evidence.

For current ordinary chemotherapy low-risk scenario, independent systematic review plus Australasian consensus is cleaner; avoid counting older and updated same-organization position papers as independent research.
